sentence: Which portrait of herself does Naila think Farah will display?

derivationStages.stageRecord: The object NP moves from the complement of display to embedded Spec-CP, leaving an A′-trace in its previously established object position. Moving the whole NP pied-pipes of herself, so the reflexive remains inside the nominal. This intermediate landing site makes extraction successive-cyclic under the GB bounding-node account of Subjacency. Think is a bridge verb, and the embedded CP is not an island. Its silent declarative C does not trigger inversion of will. The trace retains the chain's object position for theta-role, Case, and subsequent reconstruction.
derivationStages.statement: Move the whole interrogative NP to the embedded CP edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The same interrogative NP now moves from the embedded Spec-CP position established in the preceding stage to matrix Spec-CP. It leaves an intermediate A′-trace at the embedded edge, extending rather than replacing the dependency with the object trace. The matrix landing site gives the phrase scope over Naila's thinking and satisfies the matrix interrogative C. The intermediate trace is antecedent-governed through the successive-cyclic chain; the object trace is lexically governed by display. Does remains in matrix I at this stage, so subject–auxiliary inversion has not yet applied.
derivationStages.statement: Move the interrogative NP from the embedded edge to matrix Spec-CP.

values.interpretation: The reflexive identifies the individual represented in the portrait.

precedingStage.stageRecord: The interrogative nominal is the Theme complement of display. Within it, Which occupies the determiner position in Spec-NP, and the PP of herself complements portrait inside N′. The reflexive denotes the individual depicted, not the possessor of the portrait. Neither this nominal nor its PP contains a referential subject. Farah is the embedded subject, will heads embedded I, and think selects the embedded declarative CP. Naila is the matrix subject. This analysis uses the classical GB option of base-generating subjects in Spec-IP rather than introducing VP-internal subject movement. For do-support, it adopts a representation in which supportive finite does is already available in matrix I before interrogative inversion; think remains an uninflected lexical verb. The matrix interrogative C and the embedded declarative C are silent. Theta and Case dependencies are established here, but Condition A will be evaluated at LF through the wh-chain rather than imposed on this base representation.
precedingStage.statement: Construct the base structure with the interrogative nominal in the embedded object position.

sentence: Þessum börnum virðist hafa verið hjálpað.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Virðist is introduced as a V head selecting the already constructed infinitival IP, and the resulting VP is placed under matrix finite I. Its lexical -st form is treated as part of the raising predicate, not as another passive operation. In this use, virðist assigns no external theta-role, leaving matrix Spec-IP available for raising rather than introducing a thematic subject or a controller. Matrix I carries present-tense and default third-person singular features. The inflected word virðist is represented as a whole lexical terminal before head movement; movement will establish its syntactic relation to finite I without splitting or respelling the word.
derivationStages.statement: Embed the passive IP under the finite raising predicate.

values.thetaRole: one help-recipient role at the object foot

values.agreementStatus: default; the dative DP is not a nominative agreement controller

derivationStages.stageRecord: The dative DP raises from embedded Spec-IP to matrix Spec-IP, leaving an intermediate A-trace. Its movement is licensed by the non-thematic matrix subject position and the transparent infinitival IP complement. The resulting A-chain retains lexical dative and a single theta-role at its object foot; matrix I does not assign a second Case or theta-role to the DP. Independently, virðist moves from V to finite I, leaving a head trace in V. Its singular form is default agreement in the absence of a nominative agreement controller, not agreement with dative plural börnum. A declarative CP shell is then projected over the completed matrix IP. This analysis adopts a uniform CP account of Icelandic root V2: the overt subject will occupy Spec-CP and the finite head C. Both the matrix A-position and the intermediate I-position are therefore represented before those final movements.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the matrix quirky subject and finite verb position, then project the root CP.

values.interpretation: subject-initial V2; contrastive focus is not required

values.chainStatus: A-chain headed by the matrix subject position, itself linked to the pronounced DP by A-prime movement
values.thetaRole: help-recipient, assigned at the object foot

derivationStages.stageRecord: The finite I head containing virðist moves to root C, leaving an I-trace. The dative subject then moves from matrix Spec-IP to Spec-CP, leaving an A′-trace in its grammatical subject position. This final subject fronting implements root V2 and need not carry contrastive focus. It follows, rather than replaces, the A-raising derivation: the matrix subject trace heads the A-chain through embedded Spec-IP to the complement of hjálpað, while the pronounced DP binds that subject position through the A′ dependency. Each link is c-commanded by the next higher link; the lexical object trace is governed by the participle, and the intermediate subject dependencies are licensed by successive raising. No PRO, reflexive binding, or additional thematic subject is required. The final pronounced sequence is exactly Þessum börnum virðist hafa verið hjálpað, interpreted as ‘These children seem to have been helped.’ The perfect is embedded under seeming; the fronted DP remains the help-recipient rather than an experiencer selected by virðist.
derivationStages.statement: Complete subject-initial V2 and the raising-passive analysis.

sentence: どの学生も二冊の本を読まなかった。

values.interpretation: higher quantificational scope; lower external-argument position

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge copies the subject from the established external-argument position to the edge of T, satisfying T's subject requirement. The higher occurrence is pronounced, and the complete lower occurrence becomes silent. The subject's universal quantifier will be interpreted at the higher position, while its thematic dependency remains anchored in the lower position. Establishing this position separately makes the subsequent object-scope operation relative to the universal subject explicit.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the universal subject above negation.

values.interpretation: higher existential operator binds lower object variable
values.landingSite: edge of Neg below the subject

values.ordering: universal subject > existential two-book object > negation
values.reading: For each student, there is a potentially student-dependent pair of books that the student did not read.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Covert Internal Merge copies the case-marked object from its established complement position to the edge of the negative domain, below the raised universal subject. The higher object occurrence is silent, so the original object remains pronounced before the verb. At interpretation, its existential operator is interpreted in the higher occurrence and binds the object variable supplied by the lower occurrence; it does not introduce a second independent existential. This object-scope operation is assumed to apply before transfer of the verbal domain, with no intervening island or completed phase boundary. Silent declarative C completes the clause. The resulting scope is universal subject over existential object over negation: each student has a possibly different pair of books that the student did not read. The existential choice can depend on the student, unlike the shared-pair reading. Negation targets reading the pair; a stronger inference that neither member was read is not a separate syntactic derivation. The universal remains above negation, and the full stop has no supplied token position.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the distributively varying, negation-external object reading.

sentence: どの学生も二冊の本を読まなかった。

values.interpretation: higher quantificational scope; lower external-argument position

derivationStages.stageRecord: The subject undergoes Internal Merge from the previously displayed external-argument position to the edge of T. The higher copy bears the pronunciation and universal scope; the complete lower copy is silent and retains the thematic position. This movement satisfies the subject requirement associated with T. The object has not yet undergone its distinct covert scope operation.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the raised universal subject and its lower thematic copy.

values.interpretation: higher existential operator binds lower object variable
values.landingSite: outer edge of T above the universal subject

values.ordering: existential two-book object > universal subject > negation
values.reading: There is one pair of books such that every student failed to read that pair.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Covert Internal Merge copies the case-marked object from its established complement position to an outer edge of T, above the raised universal subject. The higher occurrence is silent, preserving the input's subject–object–verb order. Its existential operator is interpreted above the universal and binds the lower object variable; the pronounced lower copy is not interpreted as a second existential. As in the alternative object-raising derivation, this scope operation precedes transfer of the verbal domain. Silent declarative C then closes the clause. The result is ‘There are two books such that every student failed to read them,’ with one shared pair taking scope over all students and negation. This is distinct from selecting a potentially different pair for each student. Negation still scopes below universal どの…も; the analysis does not generate a free ‘not every student’ reading. Whether contextual knowledge strengthens failure to read the pair into reading neither member is not an additional structural ambiguity. The sentence-final punctuation is outside the supplied token list.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the shared, wide-scope two-book reading.

sentence: الكتب التي اشتراها سامر ليست هنا.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge transitive v with the verbal object, then externally merge سامر as its specifier. Samer receives the agent role here, below the position that will host the finite verb. The silent object remains the verb's complement. The resulting subject-before-verb workspace is an intermediate structure, not the relative clause's final pronunciation order.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce Samer as the relative clause's agent.

values.representation: overt moved head and silent lower trace

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verbal head raises from the complement structure established previously and adjoins to v. Its inflected lexical form, including the object suffix, moves as one opaque head. A silent head trace records the vacated position. This intermediate workspace is retained because the resulting complex v head must exist before it can raise to T.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the relative verb to transitive v.

values.representation: overt moved head and silent lower trace

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge past T above the agent-containing structure, then raise the previously constructed complex v head to T. The finite verb consequently precedes سامر, which remains in its external-argument position. T agrees with the postverbal subject and licenses nominative Case; no subject-raising requirement is imposed on this Arabic verb-initial clause. Past morphology is already contained in the overt verbal word, so abstract T introduces no additional pronounced material.
derivationStages.statement: Establish finite verb–subject order inside the relative clause.
